name: prompt-input
title: Prompt input
purpose: Provide an accessible, source-owned message composer with clear empty, ready, multiline, submitting, and rejected-submission behavior plus optional context and toolbar composition without connecting to an AI service.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Semantic form and async submission boundary.

anatomy.name: leading
anatomy.description: Optional context, selection, attachment, or mode summary.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.description: Visible input affordance and persistent accessible label relationship.

anatomy.name: toolbar
anatomy.description: Secondary controls, guidance, and primary submit alignment.

anatomy.name: toolbar-start
anatomy.description: Optional attachment, voice, model, or tool controls.

anatomy.name: submit
anatomy.description: Primary submit action with accessible name and async state.

slots.name: leading
slots.description: Context shown above the text field.

slots.name: toolbarStart
slots.description: Attachment, voice, model, or tool controls before the hint.

themes.name: light
themes.description: Graphite-neutral light field and control treatment.

themes.name: dark
themes.description: Near-black field with clear surface and focus distinction.

themes.name: high-contrast
themes.description: Strengthened field, action, disabled, and focus boundaries.

viewports.name: mobile
viewports.expectation: Toolbar wraps without covering input; controls remain touch-safe above the software keyboard.

viewports.name: tablet
viewports.expectation: Field, secondary controls, hint, and submit retain a clear order.

viewports.name: desktop
viewports.expectation: Composer remains compact and does not stretch input copy beyond useful measure.

viewports.name: wide
viewports.expectation: Maximum width and internal alignment preserve connection to the transcript.

accessibility.semantics: Uses a native form, labeled textarea, native submit button, discoverable visible guidance, and programmatically exposed disabled and submitting states; placeholder text is not the label.
keyboard: Tab reaches the text area, optional toolbar controls, and submit in visual order.
Native form submission does not override multiline text-entry or assistive-technology conventions.
Submitting prevents duplicate activation without disabling unrelated recovery navigation.
focus: The field and every toolbar action retain visible focus in all declared themes.
Submission completion or rejection does not move focus unexpectedly.
Growing and wrapping content does not cover the focused line or submit action.

motion.contract: Focus, submit, and async feedback use short color, opacity, or transform transitions; reduced motion removes nonessential movement without delaying feedback.
